title: AI-Assisted Software Engineering
subtitle: From Problem Definition to Verifiable Software Delivery

concepts.title: See the Product First: From Problem to Outcome
concepts.objective: Describe a product’s work value and verification levels through a synthetic task.
concepts.practice: Compare incomplete and complete inputs, and map requirements to evidence.
concepts.assessment: Distinguish local startup, specification checks, user acceptance and production release.

concepts.title: AI Can Help You Work, but Who Is Responsible?
concepts.objective: Separate responsibility for model generation, tool execution and human decisions.
concepts.practice: Assign requirements decisions, code generation, test execution and result review to suitable roles.
concepts.assessment: Identify who owns business rules and production release decisions.

concepts.title: How Do Personal Tools Differ from Organizational Systems?
concepts.objective: Identify new requirements when a single-user tool becomes a shared system.
concepts.practice: Compare data flows and permissions for local use and ten colleagues sharing a system.
concepts.assessment: List identity, authorization, storage and operations requirements that remain unimplemented.

concepts.title: A Learner Survey Is Also a Requirements Interview
concepts.objective: Turn a current-state survey into leads for follow-up questions.
concepts.practice: Use synthetic answers to design a survey about tool experience and work difficulties.
concepts.assessment: Separate reported answers, interpretations and hypotheses requiring interviews.

concepts.title: Tokens, Transformers and Attention
concepts.objective: Explain a language model through input units, representations and attention.
concepts.practice: Compare illustrative tokenizations of a sentence and identify attention’s role.
concepts.assessment: Avoid equating tokens with character counts or treating attention maps as proof of correct reasoning.

concepts.title: Context Windows and Long Conversations
concepts.objective: Explain how context capacity affects the information available during long tasks.
concepts.practice: Separate essential specifications, tool results and conversation history in a long task.
concepts.assessment: Propose ways to retain specifications and reconstruct context, while identifying omission risks.

concepts.title: KV Cache, Compaction, RAG and Memory
concepts.objective: Distinguish inference caches, summary compression, retrieval and persistent records.
concepts.practice: Compare the information retained and retrieved by KV Cache, Compaction, RAG and Memory.
concepts.assessment: Explain their different purposes instead of describing all four as greater memory capacity.

concepts.title: Chatbots, Workflows and Agents
concepts.objective: Distinguish chatbots, workflows and agents through control flow and tool actions.
concepts.practice: Choose structures for intake questions, fixed checks and iterative corrections.
concepts.assessment: Explain the controller, stop conditions and tool permissions without relying on product names.

concepts.title: Six Components of an Agent Harness
concepts.objective: Explain how six parts of an agent system support task execution.
concepts.practice: Map Context, Tools, Orchestration, Environment, Security and Observability.
concepts.assessment: Trace a correction task through its data, tools, environment and records.

concepts.title: Tool Calling, Sandboxes and Observability
concepts.objective: Make tool inputs, permissions and results observable within explicit boundaries.
concepts.practice: Design tool operations restricted to a named project and specify log fields.
concepts.assessment: Identify sandbox limits and security claims that logs alone cannot establish.

concepts.title: Turn a Vague Request into a Problem Statement
concepts.objective: Rewrite a requested solution as a problem with an actor and evidence of success.
concepts.practice: Draft problem.md and mark assumptions.
concepts.assessment: Let a peer identify who needs what, when, and which questions still need answers.

concepts.title: Roles, Stakeholders and Interviews
concepts.objective: Identify users, rule owners, affected people and operations roles.
concepts.practice: Write open interview questions for intake staff, reviewers and managers.
concepts.assessment: Ask about actual events without assuming a solution or presenting guesses as findings.

concepts.title: As-Is, To-Be and User Flows
concepts.objective: Describe the current and improved flows for the same task.
concepts.practice: Map entry, checking, correction, handoff and exception branches.
concepts.assessment: Show roles, triggers and recovery from missing data without mixing in deployment structure.

concepts.title: MVP, Scope and the Out-of-Scope List
concepts.objective: Choose a small, complete flow that tests the core problem.
concepts.practice: Separate first-release, deferred and excluded requirements, and define reactivation conditions.
concepts.assessment: Include missing-data handling in the MVP and explicit conditions for deferred work.

concepts.title: Success Metrics, Hypotheses and Requirement Records: How Do We Know a System Helps?
concepts.objective: Record measures, assumptions, sources and revision reasons for requirements.
concepts.practice: Add observable success conditions and a change log to problem.md.
concepts.assessment: Separate feature behavior from task improvement without inventing times or percentages.

concepts.title: How do HCI, UI and UX differ?
concepts.objective: Distinguish human–computer interaction, interface presentation and the overall experience.
concepts.practice: Give an HCI, UI and UX question about the same intake task.
concepts.assessment: Explain their different scopes without reducing UX to appearance.

concepts.title: Task Analysis and Interaction Flows
concepts.objective: Break a task into goals, actions, decisions and exceptions.
concepts.practice: List steps from receiving synthetic data through correction to export.
concepts.assessment: State start and end points, preconditions and recovery instead of listing interface components.

concepts.title: Information Architecture and Visual Priority
concepts.objective: Group information and set visual hierarchy according to the task.
concepts.practice: Arrange required fields, the main action, status and secondary settings.
concepts.assessment: Use meaningful reading and action order without conveying meaning through color or position alone.

concepts.title: Wireframes: Define Behavior Before Color
concepts.objective: Use low-fidelity sketches to show behavior and states.
concepts.practice: Create a four-state wireframe.svg with actions and feedback.
concepts.assessment: Let a peer replay the task before choosing branding or colors.

concepts.title: Progressive Disclosure, Minimalism and Essential States
concepts.objective: Decide which information must be visible now and which can be disclosed later.
concepts.practice: Compare four states and move debug settings to a secondary area.
concepts.assessment: Keep missing data, processing status and recovery methods directly recognizable.

concepts.title: Error Recovery, Accessibility and Usability
concepts.objective: Design a recoverable flow with keyboard access and text labels.
concepts.practice: Complete entry and correction with a keyboard, recording focus and error feedback.
concepts.assessment: Preserve input after errors, show focus and communicate status beyond color.

concepts.title: The Different Jobs of Prompts and Specifications
concepts.objective: Distinguish task instructions from requirements the system must maintain.
concepts.practice: Split “make a usable form” into agent instructions and acceptance requirements.
concepts.assessment: Retain the same externally observable behavior when tools change.

concepts.title: User Stories, Functional and Nonfunctional Requirements
concepts.objective: Turn user value into concrete functional and nonfunctional requirements.
concepts.practice: Write an intake user story with constraints and links to acceptance scenarios.
concepts.assessment: Identify required conditions and boundaries beyond the user-story sentence pattern.

concepts.title: Given/When/Then and Negative Acceptance
concepts.objective: Define normal and negative acceptance through conditions, actions and observable results.
concepts.practice: Write scenarios for complete, missing, blank and stale results.
concepts.assessment: Make every scenario reproducible and state forbidden outcomes explicitly.

concepts.title: SDD: Let Specifications Drive Change
concepts.objective: Update specifications, code and verification together when requirements change.
concepts.practice: Simulate adding a required field and list affected files and scenarios.
concepts.assessment: Trace the specification to the diff and rerun results, retaining the change reason.

concepts.title: OpenSpec and Lightweight Markdown Workflows
concepts.objective: Compare when OpenSpec and lightweight Markdown workflows fit.
concepts.practice: Map proposals, specification changes, tasks and verification for the same requirement.
concepts.assessment: Justify the choice without treating tool installation as completion of SDD.

modules.title: System Architecture, the Web and Security Boundaries

concepts.title: User Flows and System Architecture
concepts.objective: Distinguish the sequence of user actions from software structure.
concepts.practice: Compare a user flow and system architecture, explaining the question each answers.
concepts.assessment: Avoid treating buttons and screen steps as deployment containers.

concepts.title: C4 System Context: Start with External Relationships
concepts.objective: Use a context diagram to show people, the system and external dependencies.
concepts.practice: Draw intake staff, the checking system and their external relationships.
concepts.assessment: Label relationships with data or purpose without putting every internal function in the context view.

concepts.title: C4 Containers and the Four Levels
concepts.objective: Describe executable units and data stores with a container diagram.
concepts.practice: Show the browser, application process, storage and communication, then locate the four C4 levels.
concepts.assessment: Distinguish containers from in-process components and from Docker containers.

concepts.title: Browsers, HTTP, APIs and Data Flow
concepts.objective: Trace an action through the browser, request, processing and response.
concepts.practice: Draw checking and export data flows, marking technical assumptions.
concepts.assessment: Distinguish general HTTP/API examples from Streamlit’s actual communication without inventing endpoints.

concepts.title: Authentication, Authorization and Sessions
concepts.objective: Distinguish identity verification, access permission and sessions.
concepts.practice: Locate these controls and negative scenarios in a ten-user shared design.
concepts.assessment: Reject unauthorized access at the access boundary, beyond hiding screens, and mark unimplemented controls.

concepts.title: TLS, Secrets and Trust Boundaries
concepts.objective: Locate transport protection, secrets and trust boundaries.
concepts.practice: Mark external input, TLS termination and credential custody on an architecture diagram.
concepts.assessment: Separate TLS from authorization and keep secrets out of code and public logs.

modules.title: Working with an AI Coding Agent

concepts.title: Environment, Project Skeleton and Toolchain
concepts.objective: Establish a reproducible local project and tool environment.
concepts.practice: Follow the README to create a virtual environment and start the skeleton.
concepts.assessment: Record actual versions and startup results, stop the service and report environment failures accurately.

concepts.title: Constrain Agent Work with a Specification
concepts.objective: Constrain an agent through specifications, file scope and verification commands.
concepts.practice: Write task instructions and stop conditions for the first slice.
concepts.assessment: Make ambiguous rules trigger questions and keep changes reviewable.

concepts.title: Vertical Slice One: Build the Form
concepts.objective: Build a form slice with labels, required fields and a primary action.
concepts.practice: Implement three input fields, operate them with a keyboard and retain the diff.
concepts.assessment: Keep the form usable without claiming that an interface with no rules performs complete validation.

concepts.title: Vertical Slice Two: Validate the Data
concepts.objective: Separate completeness rules from the UI and verify them.
concepts.practice: Write missing, blank, type and length tests, then implement the rules.
concepts.assessment: Reject invalid input through direct rule calls as well as UI constraints.

concepts.title: Vertical Slice Three: Preview and Export
concepts.objective: Keep previews and exports consistent with the current input.
concepts.practice: Clear a field after a successful check, verify invalidation and revalidate before export.
concepts.assessment: Export only allowed fields and prevent complete reports when data is missing.

concepts.title: Review Diffs, Tool Records and Decisions
concepts.objective: Review agent changes through diffs, tool records and decision reasons.
concepts.practice: Compare a slice’s specification, file changes, commands and outputs.
concepts.assessment: Separate actual execution from summary inferences and exclude unrelated changes.

concepts.title: Debugging, Recovery and Small Iterations
concepts.objective: Debug with a reproducible minimal case and recover safely.
concepts.practice: Reproduce the stale-report problem, retain the failing test, fix incrementally and rerun.
concepts.assessment: Explain the cause and regression evidence while preserving unrelated work during recovery.

modules.title: Testing, Quality and Security Verification
modules.artifact: tests/, test results and peer task observations

concepts.title: Running Is Not the Same as Verified
concepts.objective: Describe software quality evidence by verification level.
concepts.practice: Separate startup, rule, interface, task and shared-user security evidence.
concepts.assessment: Support each completion claim with evidence and keep unmeasured items unverified.

concepts.title: TDD: Red, Green, Refactor
concepts.objective: Build a feedback loop that can fail through Red, Green, Refactor.
concepts.practice: Reproduce an invalid export first, then fix and refactor.
concepts.assessment: Retain failing and passing results, and preserve confirmed behavior during refactoring.

concepts.title: pytest and Business-Rule Tests
concepts.objective: Use pytest to verify pure business rules.
concepts.practice: Parameterize tests for three fields and check valid inputs, invalid inputs and export exceptions.
concepts.assessment: Cover boundaries beyond tool startup and make results reproducible.

concepts.title: Interface Tests with Streamlit AppTest
concepts.objective: Simulate Streamlit inputs and displayed results with AppTest.
concepts.practice: Test missing input, complete input and a subsequent input change.
concepts.assessment: Check feedback and download-element state while separately tracking real-browser download verification.

concepts.title: Task-Based Usability Testing
concepts.objective: Observe usability and revise assumptions through a target task.
concepts.practice: Have a peer correct missing data and export, recording where they get stuck.
concepts.assessment: Separate observation from interpretation without generalizing one trial to all users.

concepts.title: Security Negative Cases and Regression Evidence
concepts.objective: Build negative cases and regression evidence for risks.
concepts.practice: Test invalid exports, extra fields and stale results; separately specify unauthorized-read requirements.
concepts.assessment: Separate the prototype’s tested scope from unimplemented shared-user controls.

modules.title: Version Control, Delivery and Continuous Improvement
modules.artifact: README.md, Git history and demonstration evidence

concepts.title: Git, Diffs, Commits and Recovery
concepts.objective: Use Git to make changes reviewable and traceable.
concepts.practice: Review each slice’s diff, make purposeful commits and practice safe recovery.
concepts.assessment: Keep secrets and real data out of commits and connect each commit to a specification.

concepts.title: READMEs, Limits and Handoffs
concepts.objective: Write instructions and limits another person can reproduce.
concepts.practice: Have a peer start and test from a clean environment using the README.
concepts.assessment: Include the environment, commands, results, limits, stopping and cleanup.

concepts.title: Demonstrating Results and Acceptance Evidence
concepts.objective: Demonstrate engineering outcomes with artifacts and actual evidence.
concepts.practice: Use the six integration questions to trace requirements through delivery.
concepts.assessment: Show corrections and unverified work, with reproducible checks beyond screenshots.

concepts.title: Changing Technology, Continuing Engineering Responsibilities
concepts.objective: Retain requirements, permission and verification responsibilities when tools change.
concepts.practice: Compare contracts that must survive a Coding Agent or UI-framework replacement.
concepts.assessment: Propose regression scope after migration without equating a brand update with validation.
